desc: Precompute `end_max[i]` and `start_index[i]` for each index i using Kadane's algorithm (forward pass for end_max, backward pass for start_max and start_index).
Precompute `global_max` as the maximum subarray sum of the original array.
For each unique element x, collect all indices where x occurs. Generate the segments (gaps) between consecutive occurrences (including before the first and after the last).
Collect all gaps as queries (l, r). Sort the queries by l in descending order.
Sort the indices j by `start_index[j]` in descending order.
Use a Fenwick tree (or segment tree) that supports point update and range maximum query. Iterate l from n-1 down to 0:
For all j such that `start_index[j] == l`, update the Fenwick tree at position j with `end_max[j]`.
For all gaps with left endpoint l, query the Fenwick tree for the maximum in [l, r] and update the global answer.
Return the maximum of the global max and the answers from all gaps.
